audio.t: Attention, residents of Dorm Building C. Because several students have reported flu symptoms this week, the dormitory office will place hand sanitizer at every elevator and in all shared kitchens. Residents who have a fever are asked to wear a mask in common areas and to report their symptoms to the health center online. Free masks are available at the front desk until Sunday evening. Thank you for helping keep our community healthy.

questions.explain: 廣播最後說櫃台到週日晚上提供免費口罩，故選 C。乾洗手是放在電梯與共用廚房，不是櫃台；流感快篩與體溫計都沒有提到。

audio.t: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to this short health talk. I'm a nurse at the campus health center. As the weather gets colder, we usually see more students with colds and the flu, especially around midterms, when many of you are sleeping less and eating badly.

So, first, the flu vaccine. It's free for all registered students this year, but you must book a time through the student portal. Walk-ins are only accepted on Wednesday afternoons. Remember, it takes about two weeks for the vaccine to fully protect you, so please don't wait until December.

Second, if you do get sick, our clinic is open from eight thirty to five on weekdays. A doctor is available every morning, and a visit costs only one hundred fifty dollars if you show your health insurance card. If you need a sick-leave note for a class, ask the doctor during your visit. We can't write one later, after you've already recovered. Finally, wash your hands often and stay home if you have a fever. Your classmates will thank you.

questions.explain: 護理師說期中考時學生睡得少、吃得差，所以生病的人更多，故選 B。其他選項（停課、健康中心關閉、考後才打疫苗）都沒有提到。
options: Classes are often canceled during that time.
Students are more likely to get sick then.

The vaccine is only offered after midterms.

head: From: Campus Health Center <health@univ.edu.tw>
To: All Undergraduate Students
Subject: Free Flu Vaccination – Book Your Slot by November 6
passage: This year, the Health Center is offering free flu vaccines to all registered students. Vaccinations will be given from October 28 to November 13 in Room 105 of the Health Center. To reserve a time, please log in to the student portal and select "Health Services." Online booking closes on November 6.

Before your appointment, you must complete a short health questionnaire on the portal. Students who are currently running a fever will be asked to **postpone** their vaccination until they have recovered. Please also bring your student ID; without it, we cannot record your vaccination in your health file.
Students who are under 20 years old must upload a signed parental consent form. If you have questions, call extension 2210 or visit the front desk between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m.

questions.explain: 信件主旨與第一段都在說明免費流感疫苗及如何預約，故選 D。信中沒有提到新的營業時間、居家照護或更新保險。
options: To announce new opening hours of the Health Center
To explain how to treat the flu at home
To ask students to update their health insurance
To invite students to book a free vaccination

passage: Every autumn, the campus health center gets busier. Last October, it recorded more than 1,800 visits, about 30 percent more than in a typical spring month. Most students came in with colds, sore throats, or the flu. But according to center director Dr. Lin Mei-hua, a growing number arrived with a different problem: stress.

"Around midterms, we see students who haven't slept properly in days," Dr. Lin said. "Some have headaches or stomach problems, but the real cause is anxiety about grades." Under current rules, however, a sick-leave note can only be issued for physical illness, so these students often feel they have no choice but to attend class.

This semester, the Student Association has proposed a change. Under its plan, each student could take up to two "wellness days" per semester without a doctor's note. Students would simply submit a short form online at least one day in advance, and professors would not be allowed to lower participation grades for those absences.

Supporters say the policy would encourage students to rest before small problems become serious ones. "Right now, people come to class sick because they're afraid of losing points," said association president Wu Jia-hao. "That's bad for them and for everyone sitting next to them."

Not everyone is convinced. Some faculty members worry that students will use the days to extend long weekends or skip exams. In response, the proposal excludes exam days and requires students who miss a group presentation to arrange a replacement date with their professor.
The University Council will vote on the plan in December. If approved, it could take effect as early as next spring.

questions.explain: 第一、二段指出林主任發現越來越多學生是因「壓力」前來就診，故選 C。文中說秋季比春季忙，且感冒流感仍是多數，A、B 錯誤；D 沒有提到。
